key_insight: Mutually incompatible martensitic deformation gradients in Ti₇₆Nb₂₂Al₂ can support a microstructure that preserves the grain boundary and has identity macroscopic deformation.
engineering_relevance: The analysis links transformation-strain compatibility to interface patterns and shape preservation in a shape-memory alloy.
method: Analyze 12 martensitic gradients rank-one connected to austenite using the moving mask approximation.
Establish a degenerate T₁₂ configuration under unit middle eigenvalue and volume preservation, with microstructures supported on only 8 gradients.
Assess near-compatibility of gradient pairs against observed interface frequencies.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports experimental confirmation of identity macroscopic deformation and associates more nearly compatible gradient pairs with more frequently observed interfaces.
watch_item: The exact construction assumes unit middle eigenvalue and volume preservation; no deformation with gradients in the finite set almost everywhere satisfies the same boundary condition.
paper_title: Complex Martensitic Microstructures in ${\rm Ti}_{76}{\rm Nb}_{22}{\rm Al}_{2}$
